name: RoHS Directive
evidence_rating: thin: one Commission evaluation with two supporting studies
summary: The Commission's 2023 evaluation found that the Directive has reduced hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment and works well overall, including as a global benchmark, but that the processes for exemptions and new restrictions lack transparency and efficiency; it proposed moving the technical assessment to the European Chemicals Agency.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Evaluation of Directive 2011/65/EU on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment, SWD(2023) 760 (with report COM(2023) 760)
literature.title: Evaluation of Directive 2011/65/EU on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment
literature.headline: Helped reduce hazardous substances in EEE and harmonise the market; a global benchmark; exemption and restriction procedures lack transparency, efficiency and scientific robustness
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found the ban on hazardous substances in electronics effective, but its exemption procedures slow and opaque.
literature.verified: full text read (conclusions of the report)
